[[File:Erva de Passerinho (Psittacanthus calyculatus) (28084169611).jpg|thumb|right|''Psittacanthus calyculatus'']]

'''''Psittacanthus calyculatus''''' (''erva de passerinho'') is a species of [[Neotropical realm|Neotropical]] [[mistletoe]] in the family [[Loranthaceae]], native to [[Colombia]], 
[[Mexico]], the Mexican Gulf, and [[Venezuela]].<ref name=PWO/>

==Description==
''Psittacanthus calyculatus'' is hairless, with nearly terete branches.<ref name=Don/> The leaves are opposite and ovate or lanceolate, having almost no petiole, and without veins.<ref name=Don/>
The inflorescences are terminal and in groups of three yellow to scarlet flowers which have cup-shaped bracts under them.<ref name=Don/>

==Life cycle==
In October or November, the fruit matures, and is eaten by a bird, who voids the seed. By November, if the defecation site is a suitable branch, the seed may have infected the host, and initial buds will start to appear.<ref name=vas/> Vegetative growth continues, until, four years after the initial infection, the plant flowers in November, with fruit becoming mature the following year from October to February.<ref name=vas/> Thus, there are some five years required for its life-cycle.<ref name=vas/>

==Ecology==
Vasquez Collazo and Geils (2002) report eleven observed conifer hosts for ''Psittacanthus calyculatus'': ''[[Abies religiosa]]'', ''[[Pinus gordoniana]]'', ''[[Pinus lawsonii|P. lawsonii]]'', ''[[Pinus leiophylla|P. leiophylla]]'', ''[[Pinus michoacana|P. michoacana]]'', ''[[Pinus pseudostrobus|P. pseudostrobus]]'', ''[[Pinus teocote|P. teocote]]'', ''[[Pinus montezumae|P. montezumae]]'', ''[[Pinus herrerai|P. herrerai]]'', ''[[Pinus pringlei|P. pringlei]]'', and ''[[Pinus rudis|P. rudis]]''.<ref name=vas/>

At least nineteen bird species ([[insectivores]], [[omnivores]], and [[granivores]]) have been seen feeding on the fruits.<ref name=vas/>

==Taxonomy==
''Psittacanthus calyculatus'' was first described by [[Augustin Pyramus de Candolle|de Candolle]] in 1830 as ''Loranthus calyculatus'',<ref name=ipni1/><ref name=DC/> and in 1834, [[G.Don|Don]] assigned it to the new genus ''[[Psittacanthus]]''.<ref name=ipni2/><ref name=Don/>

==Etymology==
''Psittacanthos'' comes from the Greek ''psittakos'' (parrot), and the Greek ''anthos'' (flower), chosen according to Don,<ref name=Don/> possibly because of the bright colours.  ''Calyculatus'' is the Latin for 'provided with a calyculus', which is a cup-like structure below the calyx, formed by a whorl of bracts.<ref name=Stearn/>
